_doc: One entry per catalogued photograph (109 first-run records + 18 added): scope, staged flag with its basis, saved image files, camera-position statements, NPS Then-And-Now identity (image matching), registered poses and the candid verdict. Built by build_registry.py from registry_data.py and verdicts.json; no verdict here is written by a program.

photographs.title: View of Gettysburg from Cemetery Hill
photographs.creator: O'Sullivan, Timothy H., 1840-1882
photographs.why: P06: At the registered pose (East Cemetery Hill, Wiedrich monument plus 25 m east, looking to the borough) the model puts every building in a narrow band at the horizon (0.52 of the frame height) and shows no road; the photograph has the Baltimore Pike running from the lower left to the town at left centre, houses spread over the full frame width, a ridge behind them at 0.47 and a tent camp at the right. The apparent size and spread of the town differ by about a factor of 2: the camera was nearer the town and lower on the slope than assumed (sigma 150 m), and the model holds only 2023 outlines of surviving buildings. The verdict is on this pose only.

The orchard, the stone wall, the fences and the trees are not in the model; the test is not independent for the footprint.

photographs.title: [Gettysburg, Pa. Headquarters of Gen. Robert E. Lee on the Chambersburg Pike]
photographs.why: P17: The Thompson house footprint (2023 outline, default one storey) is placed south-south-west of the house with its distance read from the photograph (fitted), so its width and place agree by construction (0.26 to 0.81 against 0.19 to 0.83 of the frame). The model shows the long south facade face-on and 3.2 m high; the photograph shows a three-quarter view with the gable at the right and a 1.5-storey roof. The NPS fixes the direction (looking north across the turnpike) but not the bearing, so the difference of about 30 degrees is the assumed bearing, not a fault of the model. Nothing independent is left.

photographs.title: [Gettysburg, Pa. The Bryan house on 2d Corps line, near scene of Pickett's Charge]
photographs.why: P19: The Bryan house footprint (6.0 by 7.6 m, 1.5 storeys, 2023 outline) is placed east-south-east of the house with the distance read from the photograph (fitted): the wire box fills the frame as the house does, but taller and without roof, lean-to or bake-oven shed; nothing independent can be compared. Whether this record is the NPS Brien Farm report's photograph taken east of the house looking west is not established (caption only).

photographs.title: [Gettysburg, Pa. Breastworks on Little Round Top; Round Top in distance]
photographs.creator: O'Sullivan, Timothy H., 1840-1882
photographs.why: P09: Silhouette of Big Round Top from the assumed spot on the south slope of Little Round Top (statue point, 35 m south, heading 202 deg toward the gazetteer centre of Big Round Top): the photograph's hill has its summit at 0.38 of the frame width and 0.28 of its height with a broad right flank; the model's cone has its summit at 0.42 and 0.43, i.e. about 15 percent of the frame height (5 degrees) lower, and a narrower top. The horizontal place and the kind of silhouette agree; the vertical offset fits a camera lower on the slope than assumed (the spot is only known as the southern slope, sigma 60 m) and the forest canopy that the bare DEM lacks. Pose and terrain errors cannot be separated.

photographs.title: [Gettysburg, Pa. The center of the Federal position viewed from Little Round Top]
photographs.creator: Gardner, Alexander, 1821-1882
photographs.why: P01: Far field at the registered pose (Warren statue summit, heading 7.8 deg, 40 deg field): the model horizon sits at 0.51 of the frame height, the photograph's far ridge and groves at about 0.44 (read by eye, +-0.02), about 3 degrees higher. The landmarks the NPS names fall in the NPS order (Codori house, High Water Mark monument for the Copse, Ziegler's Grove, Cemetery Hill) but 40 to 110 px of a 480-px panel (3 to 9 degrees) left of the features they should mark, the error growing to the right, so the spacing is about 1.8 times too narrow at 40 degrees (the 30 degree render is closer: a longer lens is likely, undocumented). The boulder, pine and stump of the near field are not in the model. Pose, lens and terrain errors cannot be separated. The Patterson stand-in lies 31 degrees right of Cemetery Hill, outside any frame, so it cannot be tested (EG-11).
